$comment: Curated CROSS-STORY dependency edges over the 29 canonical stories: 'from' is a prerequisite or strong enabler of 'to'. Complements data/story-graph.json, whose builds-on edges stay inside one cluster — these edges may cross clusters and themes (API surface → openness, openness → privacy…). Every edge carries a 'why' justifying the dependency honestly (prerequisite = can't exist without; enabler = the standard vehicle for). Validated by lib/storyEdges.ts (zod) and lib/__tests__/storyEdges.test.ts (canon ids only, no duplicate of a story-graph edge, union of both files stays acyclic). Rendered by components/CapabilityDag.tsx on /global and as 'unlocks →' hints in components/StoryMap.tsx.

edges.why: A first-party CLI is the API's terminal skin — it calls the same documented endpoints. Without a public API there is nothing for an official CLI to wrap.
Headless/CI automation drives the product without its UI; the documented API (directly or via the CLI that wraps it) is the surface those scripts call.
'Everything the UI can do, the API can do' presupposes a public API to measure parity against — no API, no parity claim.
Complete, scriptable export of all your data is usually delivered through API endpoints — a public API is the standard vehicle for leaving with everything.
Official SDKs are typically generated from or maintained against the machine-readable spec — a published OpenAPI file is what keeps SDK coverage complete and current.
Official MCP servers are commonly generated from or mapped onto the machine-readable API spec — the spec is what keeps tool schemas accurate.
CI runs on every commit need an environment that can't touch production data — a sandbox is what makes headless automation safe to run continuously.
Headless runs park credentials in a CI runner's secret store where no human is watching — least-privilege scoped keys are what make that acceptable.
An automation running unattended in the background acts on standing credentials — scoping those credentials to least privilege is what bounds the blast radius.
Autonomous background automations are the rules engine grown up — the trigger/action machinery has to exist before automations can run unattended on top of it.

Source under an open license is the strongest enabler of self-hosting — you can run your own instance without waiting for a vendor-issued distribution (proprietary self-host exists, but open source makes it the default).
Running your own instance is the ultimate residency control — the data lives wherever you choose to host it, no vendor region list required.
Self-hosting keeps data on infrastructure you control — vendor-side model training can't touch what never leaves your servers.
